--- title: "Phonemic verbal fluency" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_FON_FLUIDEZ_FONOLOGICA" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_FON_FLUIDEZ_FONOLOGICA`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Fluidez fonológica*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_FON_FLUIDEZ_FONOLOGICA.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Phonemic verbal fluency, at age 5 (793 administrations in 1 cohorts). AUC .68 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2028 | | Battery | DIS-ESP | | Format | rapid naming of a series | | Items | — | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | INSTRUCCIONES: La prueba consiste en medir cuántas palabras que comience por el mismo fonema puede decir el niño o la niña en 30 segundos. Para ello, colocaremos al sujeto de forma que no vea la pantalla del ordenador. *(Spanish)* | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_ran.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework The **categorical perception** tasks (Serniclaes battery) use synthetic syllables ranging from BA to PA in voicing steps. In identification, the child says which syllable they hear; in discrimination, whether two syllables are the same or different. **Minimal pairs** ask the child to decide whether two real syllables are the same or different. They measure the precision of phonemic categories, the basis of letter–sound correspondences. **Phonological fluency** (saying, in 30 seconds, words that begin with a given phoneme) measures something else: lexical access from a sound and executive control. **What the evidence says:** - **Dyslexia shows a categorical perception deficit, clearer in discrimination.** A meta-analysis confirms the deficit compared with children of the same age and with younger readers at the same level. The effect is larger in discrimination than in identification [@noordenbos2015meta]. - **In Spanish, what fails is the boundary between categories.** In 204 Spanish children, those with dyslexia discriminated pairs that cross the phonemic boundary worse and some within-category differences better (allophonic perception) [@serniclaes2021allophonic]. That is why the total of correct responses mixes two effects of opposite sign. - **Its predictive value is modest and not entirely phonological.** In 237 children, perception at age 5½ predicted reading a year later without going through phonemic awareness. These tasks also capture decision making [@snowling2019speech]. In another study, its effect on decoding disappeared when phonological processing was controlled [@mcbridechang1997growth]. The evidence is therefore contradictory. - **Phonological fluency reflects access, not representations.** In 66 Greek children with dyslexia or developmental language disorder, word production was lower, but the size of clusters of related words was the same as in 83 controls [@mengisidou2019fluency]. **What our data show.** - **Categorical perception.** Discrimination does not predict persistent difficulty (AUC .39–.53) and identification barely does (.51–.63). This is to be expected if the total of correct responses is scored: the identification slope and between- and within-category discrimination should be computed from the item-by-item responses. - **Minimal pairs.** Low stability (ρ = .07–.39) and AUC from .45 to .69, better from age 5. Against Woodcock-Muñoz, .63–.66 at ages 6–7. - **Phonological fluency.** A single session at age 5 (793 children, almost all from Preleo schools): AUC of .68 against persistent difficulty and of .59–.62 against low comprehension. It is related to phonological awareness, letters and reading (ρ = .41–.43). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 5.3| 2011| 159|2016/17 | 793| 0| 793| 34| ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (5.3, r = .41). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .68. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .59–.62. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_FON_FLUIDEZ_FONOLOGICA_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .63 (1 time point; 225–225 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 5.3| 793| 2011| 0| 1| 1| 1| 2| 3| 5| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_FON_FLUIDEZ_FONOLOGICA_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 5.3| 793| 0.126| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.3| 790| 0.174| 0.015| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.3| 788| 0.134| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 5.3| 793| 0.036| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Phonemic verbal fluency” (code 2028; DIS-ESP battery) assesses phonemic verbal fluency. The child names a series of familiar stimuli on the screen as quickly as possible, and the examiner records correct responses and errors. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2011 cohorts it was administered in 1 session, from 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .59–.62. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
